speedrun.lead: Not yet a comparison with plain JavaScript: the speed run’s “plain” way put only three rules in JavaScript (the gnome’s step, the beavers’, the river’s level) and left every other piece Hazel’s, on 11-25 as on 11-27; it is being run again with the page’s own ⚡, every piece in JavaScript (^ticket(896)).
speedrun.body: What the runs do show: with every piece Hazel’s, the whole speed run took 27.2 s on 11-27 (588 µs a step), 0.90 s of it in the rules (3.3%), the birds alone 261,889 calls and 0.36 s; on 11-25, before the animals moved, 25.5 s, 0.34 s in the rules (1.3%). The rest of each step is the page’s JavaScript: the water, the rest of the world, the speed run’s own way-finding. The interpreter’s way did not start on 0.0.148: a library bug, found and fixed on a trial branch (^ticket(896): the interpreter’s calls of a function typed on its let took whole numbers as Ints where Floats are declared, and stopped).
speedrun.cap: Gnome world’s speed run in headless Chrome on GitHub’s machines (node/world-speedrun.mjs): 11-25 at bbfde10 (^report(65)) and 11-27 at 0.0.148, 5e43910 (run 46025660460). Its “plain” bars are not plain JavaScript: only the gnome’s step, the beavers’ and the river’s level were swapped; the other pieces stayed Hazel’s (^ticket(896)). The worlds of the two days differ, so compare within a day.
